as_told.title: Former NASA engineer on electromagnetic anomalies near Bermuda Triangle

plain: The stretch of Atlantic known as the Bermuda Triangle is said to show real, measurable anomalies. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, tells Michels, "there's data there's evidence of anomalies" there, speaking as someone who knows the Navy's view of the oceans. On another episode Michels repeats what a former NASA engineer told him: that "there is a little patch around the Bermuda Triangle" with "just tons of electromagnetic anomalies going on." Gallaudet speaks of evidence in general terms, while the engineer's version is specifically electromagnetic. If true, it would give an old legend something physical behind it.
